data.body:
LOOP ITERATION 4. Review round 6: BLOCK, 2 findings — but both state the SAME defect, and it was
mine: inbound_fields.py is required by the triage AND by an explicit AC, yet was absent from the Scope
file list. An implementer following Scope would not have known to touch it, and the
reporter-idempotence AC cannot pass without it.

Cause: I added the _identity_of requirement to the triage and the ACs two rounds ago and never
propagated it to Scope. Same class as round 4's finding (Scope contradicting Approach). Scope is the
section I keep forgetting to update, which is worth naming as a personal failure mode rather than
treating as two unrelated slips.

FIXED:
 * Added src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py to Scope, with the reason (_identity_of
   at :163 reads accountId ONLY, so a DC reporter yields account_id=None and the mutation re-emits
   forever) and the note that it is a CORE module, not an adapter one — the reviewer hedged 'or a
   shared path', and the distinction matters because the shape is vendor-neutral and both adapters
   feed it.
 * Tightened dispatch_apply_phases.py from 'ONLY if the verdict goes that way' to an explicit
   NOT MODIFIED, since the verdict is now resolved. Leaving a conditional file in Scope after the
   condition is settled is an invitation to edit it.
 * Rewrote file_impact to match Scope exactly (8 paths), so the file-impact-coverage gate and the plan
   agree.

Round 6 also carried NO repeat of the disputed add_issue_property finding from round 5 — the citation
of the library source path and method body appears to have settled it, which is the outcome I wanted:
the claim is now checkable from the plan rather than requiring the reviewer to resolve an installed
package. Re-review running.
